title: Distributed Systems & Failure-Tolerant Architecture
summary: Reason about systems where nodes fail independently, messages are delayed/duplicated/lost and global state is never perfectly visible.

modules.title: Distributed-system failure model
modules.summary: Internalize uncertainty, partial failure and the limits of synchronous mental models.
modules.why: A network call can fail before, during or after the remote side commits work; callers often cannot know which.

units.title: Partial failure & independent processes
units.summary: Understand why one component can fail while the rest keep running.
units.challenge: Inject crash, pause and partition into a two-service workflow and record distinct symptoms.
units.evidence: Failure taxonomy with observed caller/remote state.

units.title: Unknown outcomes & the two-generals intuition
units.summary: Reason about operations whose response was lost after possible commit.
units.challenge: Model a money-transfer-like request where timeout occurs at every network/commit point.
units.evidence: State-space diagram showing what the caller can and cannot know.

units.title: Failure detectors, synchrony assumptions & impossibility intuition
units.summary: Know which guarantees require timing/availability assumptions.
units.challenge: Review a leader-election design that equates timeout with death and identify split-brain risk.
units.evidence: Assumptions list and safety/liveness trade-off explanation.

modules.title: Time, causality & distributed identifiers
modules.summary: Separate wall-clock time from event causality and uniqueness.
modules.why: Clock skew can corrupt ordering, leases and IDs if time is treated as universally true.

units.title: Wall clocks, monotonic clocks & skew
units.summary: Use clocks for the correct purpose and anticipate drift/jumps.
units.challenge: Design timeout/elapsed-time logic that survives wall-clock adjustment.
units.evidence: Clock API choice table and skew test.

units.title: Lamport & vector-clock causality
units.summary: Order causally related events without relying on synchronized physical clocks.
units.challenge: Track concurrent edits from three replicas and identify causal vs concurrent updates.
units.evidence: Clock traces and conflict classification.

units.title: UUID, ULID & Snowflake-style IDs
units.summary: Generate unique identifiers under throughput and ordering constraints.
units.challenge: Choose an ID scheme for globally created tasks and analyze DB-index/write effects.
units.evidence: ID decision record including collision/order/privacy trade-offs.

modules.title: Consistency models & client guarantees
modules.summary: Name the guarantees users and services observe instead of saying only strong/eventual.
modules.why: Different product workflows need different guarantees, and stronger consistency has latency/availability costs.

units.title: Linearizability vs serializability
units.summary: Separate real-time single-object/system consistency from transaction schedule correctness.
units.challenge: Classify guarantees for a serializable DB with asynchronous replicas.
units.evidence: Examples showing why the terms are not interchangeable.

units.title: Eventual consistency & session guarantees
units.summary: Define acceptable convergence and user-visible monotonicity.
units.challenge: Design profile/settings reads across replicas so users do not see their own update disappear.
units.evidence: Routing/session strategy with anomaly examples.

units.title: Causal consistency
units.summary: Preserve cause-before-effect while allowing unrelated concurrency.
units.challenge: Design comment/reply visibility where replies must not appear before parent comments.
units.evidence: Causal dependency model and allowed reordering.

modules.title: Replication models & conflict handling
modules.summary: Compare leader-based, multi-leader and leaderless replication under failure and locality.
modules.why: Replication is the core mechanism behind availability, durability and read scale—but creates divergence.

units.title: Single-leader replication
units.summary: Understand write leadership, follower lag and failover.
units.challenge: Design primary/replica placement and read policy for low-latency global reads.
units.evidence: Stale-read/failover trade-off matrix.

units.title: Multi-leader replication & conflicts
units.summary: Handle concurrent writes across locations without pretending conflicts vanish.
units.challenge: Design two-region editable user preferences and define conflict semantics per field.
units.evidence: Conflict examples and resolution policy.

units.title: Leaderless replication, read repair & anti-entropy
units.summary: Use quorum-style reads/writes while repairing divergent replicas.
units.challenge: Walk through replica outage/recovery with concurrent writes.
units.evidence: Replica state timeline and repair process.

modules.title: CAP, PACELC & quorum reasoning
modules.summary: Use consistency/availability/latency models precisely rather than as slogans.
modules.why: Architectural trade-offs occur both during partitions and during normal operation.

units.title: CAP theorem precisely
units.summary: Understand the partition scenario and what availability/consistency mean in CAP.
units.challenge: Classify several systems only after stating their partition behaviour and guarantee definition.
units.evidence: CAP analyses with assumptions instead of labels only.

units.title: PACELC & normal-operation trade-offs
units.summary: Include latency vs consistency when there is no partition.
units.challenge: Compare synchronous global quorum and local-write eventual designs.
units.evidence: Latency budget plus consistency matrix.

units.title: Read/write quorums & overlap
units.summary: Reason about R, W, N and replica overlap while respecting failure caveats.
units.challenge: Calculate quorum configurations and simulate failed/stale replicas.
units.evidence: Configuration table with read/write availability and latency implications.

modules.title: Consensus, Raft & replicated state machines
modules.summary: Understand how a group agrees on an ordered log despite node failures.
modules.why: Consensus underpins metadata stores, leader election and many databases; using it blindly can centralize latency/availability bottlenecks.

units.title: Consensus problem & replicated state machine
units.summary: Understand agreement, validity and fault assumptions.
units.challenge: Explain why simply broadcasting writes cannot guarantee one ordered history under failure.
units.evidence: Safety/liveness explanation with counterexample.

units.title: Raft election & log replication
units.summary: Follow terms, voting, leader election and log commitment.
units.challenge: Step through leader failure and competing candidates using a Raft visualization/paper.
units.evidence: Annotated event timeline with committed/uncommitted entries.

units.title: Consensus operational trade-offs
units.summary: Understand quorum loss, membership change and latency implications.
units.challenge: Choose etcd/consensus-node placement across 3 regions and analyze region/network failure.
units.evidence: Placement ADR with quorum/latency table.

modules.title: Leader election, locks, leases & fencing
modules.summary: Coordinate exclusive ownership without stale actors corrupting state.
modules.why: Distributed locks fail when pause/partition lets an expired holder continue acting.

units.title: Leader election & single-owner tasks
units.summary: Assign one active coordinator while planning for failure and transition.
units.challenge: Design one active scheduler leader with controlled failover.
units.evidence: Election state machine and duplicate-leader failure analysis.

units.title: Distributed locks & leases
units.summary: Distinguish mutual-exclusion intent from time-bounded ownership evidence.
units.challenge: Pause a lock holder beyond lease expiry and show why it may still write.
units.evidence: Stale-holder timeline demonstrating unsafe lock-only design.

units.title: Fencing tokens & stale-owner rejection
units.summary: Make the protected resource reject operations from expired owners.
units.challenge: Implement a lease/token simulation where resource accepts only newest token.
units.evidence: Test proving resumed stale holder cannot corrupt state.

modules.title: Partitioning, sharding & rebalancing
modules.summary: Scale state horizontally while managing hotspots, routing and movement.
modules.why: A shard key is one of the hardest-to-change architecture decisions once data/traffic grow.

units.title: Range, hash & directory partitioning
units.summary: Choose partition functions from access locality and hotspot risk.
units.challenge: Choose partition strategies for time-series, users and tenants.
units.evidence: Workload/access-pattern decision table.

units.title: Consistent hashing & virtual nodes
units.summary: Reduce remapping when nodes join/leave distributed caches/stores.
units.challenge: Implement a small consistent-hash ring and measure key movement on node changes.
units.evidence: Simulation results and balance analysis.

units.title: Hot partitions, resharding & online movement
units.summary: Detect skew and move ownership while serving traffic.
units.challenge: Design tenant sharding where one tenant becomes 100x larger than peers.
units.evidence: Resharding/migration plan with traffic continuity.

modules.title: Distributed transactions & atomic commit
modules.summary: Understand coordination protocols for all-or-nothing changes across participants.
modules.why: Atomic commit can provide strong guarantees but couples availability and latency to all participants/coordinator.

units.title: Two-phase commit
units.summary: Understand prepare/commit and coordinator/participant failure states.
units.challenge: Step through coordinator crash after participants prepare.
units.evidence: 2PC state machine with recovery ambiguity.

units.title: XA-style atomicity & operational trade-offs
units.summary: Understand why cross-resource atomic transactions are uncommon in microservice architecture.
units.challenge: Compare 2PC with saga for inventory+payment workflow.
units.evidence: Decision matrix by invariant, latency and failure tolerance.

units.title: Atomic commit vs consensus
units.summary: Distinguish agreeing on a value/log from committing a transaction across participants.
units.challenge: Explain why Raft does not automatically make arbitrary cross-service transactions atomic.
units.evidence: Concept comparison with concrete counterexample.

modules.title: Sagas, compensations & reconciliation
modules.summary: Coordinate long business workflows with explicit intermediate states and repair paths.
modules.why: Many distributed workflows cannot be atomically rolled back; business compensation and reconciliation become first-class design.

units.title: Saga state machines & compensations
units.summary: Represent each step, outcome and compensation explicitly.
units.challenge: Model order/payment/reservation workflow with failure at every step.
units.evidence: Saga state machine including manual-recovery states.

units.title: Orchestrated sagas & workflow engines
units.summary: Centralize workflow state/visibility while keeping domain ownership clear.
units.challenge: Design a durable orchestrator that survives process restart mid-workflow.
units.evidence: Workflow data model and replay/retry policy.

units.title: Reconciliation & repair jobs
units.summary: Detect impossible/partial states and converge systems after missed events or defects.
units.challenge: Design a daily reconciliation between billing and subscription state with safe repair.
units.evidence: Invariant queries, discrepancy states and repair runbook.

modules.title: Timeouts, retries, circuit breakers & bulkheads
modules.summary: Stop local dependency failure from cascading into system-wide failure.
modules.why: Naive retries and long waits multiply load during outages.

units.title: Timeouts & end-to-end latency budgets
units.summary: Bound waiting time at every dependency while preserving caller budget.
units.challenge: Allocate a 500ms user-request budget across three downstream calls.
units.evidence: Timeout/deadline budget and induced-slowdown test.

units.title: Retries, backoff & jitter
units.summary: Retry only safe/transient operations without synchronized storms.
units.challenge: Simulate 100 clients retrying one failing dependency with/without jitter.
units.evidence: Traffic graph showing herd reduction.

units.title: Circuit breakers, bulkheads & graceful degradation
units.summary: Contain failures and shed optional work before critical paths collapse.
units.challenge: Make search failure not exhaust checkout/profile capacity in a shared service.
units.evidence: Isolation architecture and failure-injection results.

modules.title: Rate limiting, quotas, admission & load shedding
modules.summary: Control demand at boundaries so overload becomes predictable rejection rather than collapse.
modules.why: Capacity protection is part of correctness for shared and multi-tenant systems.

units.title: Fixed/sliding windows, token & leaky buckets
units.summary: Understand limiter fairness, burst behaviour and state cost.
units.challenge: Implement token bucket and sliding-window variants and test burst boundaries.
units.evidence: Correctness/performance comparison.

units.title: Distributed rate limiting
units.summary: Coordinate limits across many app instances without a fragile central bottleneck.
units.challenge: Design tenant/API limits across 50 instances and two regions.
units.evidence: Consistency/availability architecture and outage policy.

units.title: Concurrency limits, admission control & load shedding
units.summary: Protect constrained resources when queued work itself becomes harmful.
units.challenge: Protect a DB-backed API under overload by bounding concurrent requests.
units.evidence: Latency/error curves before/after admission control.

modules.title: Service discovery & dynamic configuration
modules.summary: Find changing service endpoints and roll configuration safely across a distributed fleet.
modules.why: Dynamic infrastructure makes endpoint/config state distributed and eventually consistent.

units.title: DNS, registry & proxy-based discovery
units.summary: Compare client-side, server-side and DNS-based endpoint discovery.
units.challenge: Design discovery for dynamic instances and explain stale-record behaviour.
units.evidence: Request path and endpoint-refresh strategy.

units.title: Dynamic configuration & safe rollout
units.summary: Change runtime behaviour with validation, targeting and rollback.
units.challenge: Roll out a timeout/config change to 1%, 10%, 100% with automatic rollback criteria.
units.evidence: Config rollout protocol and audit model.

units.title: Feature flags as distributed control plane
units.summary: Understand evaluation consistency, stale flags and lifecycle debt.
units.challenge: Design a globally distributed kill switch with bounded propagation delay.
units.evidence: Flag architecture and stale-control risk analysis.

modules.title: Multi-region consistency, failover & disaster recovery
modules.summary: Design across regions with explicit latency, data placement and failure objectives.
modules.why: Regions are not just bigger availability zones; distance creates unavoidable latency and partition choices.

units.title: Active-passive vs active-active
units.summary: Choose regional serving/write topology from RTO, latency and conflict needs.
units.challenge: Design three regional topologies for the same product with different RTO/cost targets.
units.evidence: Topology comparison and failover sequence.

units.title: Global data placement, residency & replication
units.summary: Place data according to user latency, sovereignty and consistency constraints.
units.challenge: Serve EU/US tenants with residency constraints and global collaboration features.
units.evidence: Data map and cross-region operation rules.

units.title: Regional evacuation & DR exercises
units.summary: Plan and test the operational act of moving traffic/data during regional loss.
units.challenge: Run a tabletop region-loss exercise including hidden single-region dependencies.
units.evidence: DR runbook, dependency inventory and measured recovery plan.

modules.title: Real-time synchronization, OT & CRDTs
modules.summary: Keep collaborative state useful under concurrent edits, reconnect and multi-device operation.
modules.why: Real-time products must define ordering/conflict semantics rather than hoping events arrive in order.

units.title: Presence, delivery receipts & reconnect
units.summary: Model ephemeral vs durable real-time state and reconnect catch-up.
units.challenge: Design chat presence/messages that tolerate mobile disconnects and multi-device sessions.
units.evidence: State model separating ephemeral and durable data.

units.title: Ordering & conflict-resolution semantics
units.summary: Define what happens when concurrent operations cannot share one global order cheaply.
units.challenge: Resolve concurrent task-title/description edits under offline clients.
units.evidence: Conflict policy and examples of accepted/rejected merges.

units.title: Operational Transformation & CRDT concepts
units.summary: Understand convergence approaches for collaborative documents.
units.challenge: Implement or simulate a simple grow-only/set/text CRDT and compare with central sequencing.
units.evidence: Concurrent-operation examples proving convergence and noting metadata cost.
